description: The COMPLETE state of a multi-agent run at one moment: the agents taking part, the work each of them did and the handoffs between them — plus the Sequence the snapshot includes. A snapshot is what a lane surface renders; it never polls and never mutates. A deep link, a reload and the repair after a gap all produce a new snapshot and the surface simply draws it, which is why Apply returns a NEW value instead of editing this one. The sequence is the number the event stream re-bases on: everything up to it is already contained here. All three lists may be empty and a null list is normalised to an empty one, so a component never has to null-check the host's data. A block whose agent the snapshot does not declare still renders (a lane is appended, named through the localized fallback), because dropping a host's work would make the surface lie by omission.

members.name: Sequence
members.description: The sequence this snapshot includes — the baseline an event stream starts from. Zero (the default) means the host does not track sequences for snapshots, which is legal: the stream then starts without a baseline and accepts the run's first event.

members.name: Agents
members.description: The agents taking part, in the order the lanes are drawn. An agent declared here keeps its position even when it has no work; empty is legal (an empty run).

members.name: Blocks
members.description: The work blocks of the run, in any order — a layout orders them by time and ignores a duplicate id after the first. A block whose agent is not declared still renders, in a lane appended after the declared ones, so a run is never silently incomplete.

members.name: Handoffs
members.description: The handoffs between agents. A link that cannot be resolved to two lanes is skipped by a layout and counted (UnresolvedHandoffCount) instead of guessed; the table alternative still lists every link.

members.name: Apply
members.description: Folds an incremental batch into this snapshot and returns the result as a NEW value; this instance is never modified. The batch is expected to be the tail the shared AgentEventStream accepted, so no ordering or de-duplication happens here — that is the stream's job, once, for every surface. Sequence is NOT changed: it describes the snapshot that was loaded, not the events applied on top of it.
